lore_summary.en: Ferdowsi's Alexander carries both philosophy and a sword. He is Iranian by a twist of blood — and the world bows.
lore_summary.fa: اسکندر ذوالقرنین با شکست دادن دارا بر ایران دست یافت، اما آشکار شد که نیمه‌برادر او بوده. او جهان را فتح کرد، در جستجوی آب حیات بود و به سرزمین‌های دور رفت. وقتی جوان درگذشت، خواست دستانش از کفن بیرون باشد — تا نشان دهد که از جهان هیچ نبرده است.

scenes.body_en: Sekandar arrived in Iran not merely as a conqueror but as something stranger — a man who claimed to belong to the country he was taking apart. The Shahnameh carries a tradition that his mother was the daughter of Darab, sent away in secret because her breath smelled of herbs and the king found her disagreeable. Philip of Macedon had taken her in, married her, and Sekandar was born. This made him the half-brother of Dara, the man he had just defeated in battle. He had not known it until Dara lay dying.

That knowledge changed the shape of everything. Sekandar wept over Dara's body and swore vengeance on the two ministers who had stabbed their own king to end the war quickly. He executed them. He took Dara's daughter Roshanak as his wife, absorbing the Achaemenid line rather than erasing it. The chronicle does not let him be a pure destroyer. He arrives carrying Iranian blood, and he acts on it.

What followed was a life of movement — east and east and east again, through the known world and past its edges. Sekandar did not rest the way other kings rested. He met philosophers and debated them. He descended into the sea in a glass vessel to observe what lived in the deep. He sought the Well of Immortality in the Land of Darkness, sending his cook ahead to prepare food — and it was the cook, not Sekandar, who accidentally drank from the spring when a dried fish came back to life in his hands. The king came close to living forever but did not reach it.

He is called Two-Horned — Dhul-Qarnayn — though the Shahnameh does not settle on why. Some say it was because he ruled both East and West. Some say it was a helmet. Some say it was a mark of the divine. The ambiguity is kept. Ferdowsi was not interested in resolving it.

When Sekandar died, he was young enough that it seemed like an error. He asked that he be carried to his tomb with his hands outside the shroud, open and empty. He had conquered the world. He was taking nothing out of it. The philosophers who followed him were supposed to speak at his burial and explain what his life had meant. One by one, they refused. None of them had anything to say that would not sound hollow next to the open hands.

battle.intro_en: Ferdowsi's Alexander is Iranian by a twist of genealogy and world-conqueror by ambition. He is the most complicated figure in the chronicle's second half. To face this gate you must understand what the Shahnameh does with its most famous foreign king.
battle.intro_fa: اسکندرِ فردوسی از رهگذرِ تباری پیچیده ایرانی است و از راهِ بلندپروازی جهانگشا. او پیچیده‌ترین چهره‌ی نیمه‌ی دومِ دفتر است. برای مواجهه با این دروازه باید بفهمی شاهنامه با مشهورترین شاهِ بیگانه‌اش چه می‌کند.

battle.intro_tg: Искандари Фирдавсӣ аз роҳи печи насабномавӣ эронӣ ва аз роҳи баландпарвозӣ ҷаҳонгушо аст. Ӯ мураккабтарин чеҳраи нимаи дуввуми солнома аст. Барои рӯбарӯ шудан бо ин дарвоза бояд бифаҳмӣ Шоҳнома бо машҳуртарин шоҳи бегонааш чӣ мекунад.

codex.summary_en: Ferdowsi gives Alexander Iranian lineage by making him the son of Darab and a Greek princess — sent home before Alexander's birth. This is a narrative solution to a structural problem: how does a chronicle of Iranian kingship absorb the man who destroyed that kingship? The answer is genealogy. Alexander becomes Iranian by blood, which means his conquest is not a foreign erasure but a civil tragedy — painful, not alien. He weeps over Dara's body, and his grief is real grief.
codex.summary_fa: فردوسی به اسکندر تبارِ ایرانی می‌دهد — پسرِ داراب و شاهزاده‌ای یونانی. این راه‌حلِ روایی برای مشکلِ ساختاری است: چگونه تاریخِ شاهانِ ایرانی مردی را جذب کند که آن شاهی را نابود کرد؟

codex.summary_en: Alexander holds Dara as he dies and weeps. This is the Shahnameh's most precise statement about what distinguishes Alexander from its simple villains. Simple villains do not grieve what they destroy. Alexander does. The conqueror who weeps is not absolved. But he is not dismissed either. The Shahnameh holds him in a more uncomfortable category: the person who understood what they destroyed only after they had destroyed it.
codex.summary_fa: اسکندر دارا را در آغوش می‌گیرد و گریه می‌کند. فاتحی که عزادار می‌شود بخشوده نیست — اما رد هم نمی‌شود. شاهنامه او را در دسته‌ای ناراحت‌تر نگه می‌دارد.

codex.summary_en: Alexander is buried with his hands open, extended outside his shroud, so the world can see they are empty. He who owned everything holds nothing. Ferdowsi places this image at the point in the chronicle where it carries maximum weight: the most successful conqueror of the second half, at the moment of burial, demonstrating the same truth that Jamshid and Kay Kavus and Hormuz failed to learn while they were alive.
codex.summary_fa: اسکندر با دستانِ باز به خاک سپرده می‌شود تا دنیا ببیند خالی‌اند. موفق‌ترین فاتحِ نیمه‌ی دوم همان حقیقتی را نشان می‌دهد که جمشید و کی‌کاووس در زندگی یاد نگرفتند.

codex.title_fa: تبار در برابرِ قدرت به عنوانِ مشروعیت
codex.summary_en: The Alexander chapter is the Shahnameh's fullest exploration of what makes a ruler legitimate. Dara had lineage but lost power. Alexander had power and Ferdowsi gave him lineage to compensate. Mahmud of Ghazni — Ferdowsi's patron — had power and no legitimate lineage in the Iranian sense. The mirror is clear: Ferdowsi is writing about Mahmud by writing about Alexander. The question 'can conquest create legitimacy?' is posed through story and left for the court to feel without being told to.
codex.summary_fa: دارا تبار داشت اما قدرت را از دست داد. اسکندر قدرت داشت و فردوسی تبار به او داد. آینه روشن است: فردوسی درباره‌ی محمود می‌نویسد با نوشتن درباره‌ی اسکندر.

codex.summary_en: Alexander reaches the edge of the world and searches for the water of life. He does not find it. This quest is the Shahnameh's statement about the limits of conquest: a man can take every kingdom and still cannot take the one thing every human being wants. The world's boundary is the point at which power ends and human mortality begins.
codex.summary_fa: اسکندر به لبه‌ی دنیا می‌رسد و آبِ زندگی را نمی‌یابد. مرزِ دنیا ادعایِ جغرافیایی نیست — جایی است که قدرت پایان می‌یابد و فانی بودنِ انسانی آغاز می‌شود.

codex.summary_en: Alexander is the last foreign figure the Shahnameh absorbs into its Iranian world. After him the chronicle's kings are Sasanian — internal conflicts, not external absorption. By giving Alexander Iranian blood and Iranian grief, Ferdowsi demonstrates that the Iranian world can survive invasion if it can convert the invader into someone who carries Iranian sorrow. This is not triumphalism — Alexander still destroyed what he found. It is the chronicle's theory of cultural survival: a civilization that can make the conqueror weep for what he conquered has not entirely lost.
codex.summary_fa: اسکندر آخرین چهره‌ی بیگانه‌ای است که شاهنامه او را جذب می‌کند. تمدنی که می‌تواند فاتح را به گریه برای آنچه فتح کرده وا دارد کاملاً نباخته است.
